summary: Intermittent dedicated-pool throughput collapse during short burst traffic due to long-lived ephemeral batchers
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightNote reports repeated p99/p50 throughput collapses in their reserved dedicated pool that correlate with short bursty traffic patterns from their webhooks. Impact: production API responses slowed and several timeouts observed in their app (fail-open fallback used).

Impact:
- Customer-facing model endpoints saw a 60-90% drop in tokens/sec for 3-7 minute windows during small spiky bursts (100-400 small requests/sec).
- Several requests timed out at client after 8s (customer set strict client timeout).
- No large-scale GPU failures or OOMs reported.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserve-3 (8x A100s, mixed-tenancy), region us-east-1, pool autoprovision enabled.
- Customer traffic pattern: many short streams (~8-40 tokens) with high concurrency; they use streaming responses and model pin redwood-7b-v1.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Send 300 concurrent short-stream requests with average length 20 tokens to pinned route for 5 minutes.
2) Observe throughput and p99 latency in console under customer route.
3) Reduce concurrency to 50 and observe recovery.

Observed behavior:
- Rapid drop in aggregate token throughput a few minutes after burst starts.
- Autoscaler attempts to add capacity but GPU allocation lag >90s; in-flight batching stalls and slot fragmentation increases.
- KV-cache entries growth from long-lived ephemeral batchers (each stream pinned small KV state) produced uneven memory fragmentation across GPUs.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should provision additional slots within configured lead time (<=30s) for burst policy, or runtime should gracefully shed/serialize to maintain steady p50/p99 within SLO.

Relevant logs/metrics attached by customer (excerpt):
- scheduler: queue_depth spiking, slot_allocation_waits: 1.6m avg, allocation_failures: 0.
- autoscaler: scale_event_start -> provision_compute_request -> delayed due to vGPU allocation lag documented in cloud provider metrics.
- runtime: kv_cache_entries per-gpu: [350K, 42K, 410K, 47K, ...] indicating heavy imbalance.

Notes: No configuration changes on customer side before the incidents. Customer is on dedicated plan with autoprovision and uses conservative batcher settings in their client SDK.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:22 UTC - Aisha Khan (Support): Escalated to SRE after initial triage. Customer reports repeatable window; providing console links and sample traffic script.

2026-03-10 12:03 UTC - Diego Morales (SRE): Confirmed burst reproduction in internal testbed using customer's traffic script. Observed allocation lead times ~95-120s and per-GPU kv_cache skew. Opening deeper investigation with serving-runtime and autoscaler owners.

2026-03-10 14:40 UTC - Priya Patel (Serving Runtime): Found that short-streams keep per-stream KV cache pinned until stream termination and our slot packing logic delays eviction. This leads to many smallholders that block efficient batch packing and cause slot fragmentation.

2026-03-11 09:15 UTC - Diego Morales (SRE): Temporarily applied runtime config tweak for BrightNote route to aggressively cap per-stream KV cache retention to 2s after stream end. Immediately observed improved slot reuse and throughput recovery in customer pool.

2026-03-11 16:05 UTC - Evelyn Zhang (Autoscaler): Cloud provider reported transient vGPU placement latency due to rack maintenance; autoscaler retry backoff contributed to >60s additional lead time. Working on parallelizing placement and reducing backoff for dedicated pools.
2026-03-12 10:30 UTC - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer confirmed latency and timeouts stopped after the temporary runtime change; happy with workaround. Requested timeline for permanent fix.

2026-03-12 11:45 UTC - Diego Morales (SRE): Marking as resolved after merged fixes: hotfix to cap KV retention per-stream and autoscaler PR to parallelize placement requests. Follow-ups scheduled: regression test and runbook update assigned to INT-3382.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Short bursty streams create many short-lived KV holders; our slot packing considers KS cache state and avoids reassigning slots with non-zero KV, causing fragmentation.
Hypothesis 2: Autoscaler placement latency is amplified when cloud-side rack maintenance reduces immediate vGPU capacity, causing lead times much longer than our configured burst SLA.

Evidence: Internal test reproductions show per-GPU kv_cache_entry skew and slot utilization dropping by 70% during bursts. Cloud provider logs show placement throttling in same AZ for ~7 minutes concurrent with incidents.
Temporary mitigation verified: limiting per-stream KV retention to 2s reduces fragmentation and recovers throughput even while autoscaler is still provisioning additional GPUs.

Permanent fixes proposed: 1) runtime patch to cap and opportunistically shrink KV state for tiny streams; 2) autoscaler improvement to parallelize placement attempts and reduce exponential backoff on dedicated pools; 3) add autoscaler metric alert for placement lead time >30s.
resolution:
Root cause: Combination of (A) slot fragmentation caused by many short-lived streams holding KV cache entries and (B) transient cloud-side vGPU placement latency that extended autoscaler lead times. Fixes applied: (1) Hotfix deployed to serving-runtime to aggressively cap per-stream KV retention for streams <50 tokens and opportunistically compact KV state post-response. (2) Autoscaler PR merged to parallelize placement and lower backoff for dedicated pools (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145). (3) Updated runbook and added alerting for placement_lead_time > 30s.

Customer impact: BrightNote saw restored throughput and no further timeouts after hotfix. Follow-ups: regression tests scheduled (INT-3382), postmortem doc to be published to the incidents space, and product decision to add a per-route knob to control aggressive KV compaction.
